It manages role-based access control through admin/librarian/super-librarian usergroups, handles user account administration and people lookup, enforces content moderation policies including spam filtering and IP blocking, and provides operational capabilities like git pulls, template reloading, and debugger attachment. The plugin also oversees critical data synchronization between Open Library and Archive.org, manages batch import queues, controls catalog permissions and solr indexing, and provides system monitoring through memory profiling and Graphite metrics visualization. Built on a registration pattern where admin pages are registered via `register_admin_page()` and routed through a central `/admin` dispatcher, the plugin enforces access control at the delegate level, ensuring only authorized users can access sensitive administrative functions. Key files include code.py (main handlers), memory.py (profiling utilities), mem.py (memory inspection UI), graphs.py (metrics visualization), and services.py (Nagios integration).

agents.name: book_and_import_operations
agents.overall_context: Open Library book data operations and import API plugin. Manages book-related functionality and provides APIs for importing book data into the system. This agent handles both the book plugin layer and the import API that feeds data into the catalog.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage Open Library's book data operations and import infrastructure. The **books plugin** (openlibrary/plugins/books/) provides public-facing APIs for querying book metadata: the `/api/books` endpoint supports dynamic lookups by multiple bibliographic identifiers (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC, OCAID, OLID), while the Hathi-style volume APIs (`/api/volumes/`) offer brief and full format responses compatible with HathiTrust standards. The **importapi plugin** (openlibrary/plugins/importapi/) handles the inbound data pipeline, accepting book metadata in five formats—RDF/XML, OPDS/Atom, MARC binary, MARC XML, and JSON—and normalizing them through a unified `import_edition_builder` into standardized edition dictionaries suitable for catalog ingestion. Both plugins follow a consistent pattern: flexible input parsing with format detection, data normalization, and validation using Pydantic models that enforce required fields (title, authors, publishers, publish_date, source_records). Key files include code.py entry points for both plugins, format-specific parsers (import_rdf.py, import_opds.py), and the edition builder that abstracts field mapping complexity across heterogeneous sources.

agents.name: search_and_discovery
agents.overall_context: Open Library work search and discovery plugin. Provides search functionality for works within the Open Library system, enabling users to discover and find books and related content.
agents.job_description: The Work Search and Discovery plugin manages search and discovery functionality for Open Library's catalog of works, authors, and subjects. It provides a Solr-based search backend with sophisticated query processing, including field name mapping, faceted search, sorting, and query escaping for security. The plugin exposes multiple autocomplete endpoints (works, authors, subjects, languages) that support OLID detection and fallback to database fetches when the Solr index is stale. Core components include SearchScheme base class and specialized schemes for works, authors, and subjects that define searchable fields, facets, and sort options; a main search handler in code.py that processes queries and formats results; and subject page rendering for person, place, time, and subject types. Key patterns include luqum-based query parsing, user-friendly field name mapping to Solr fields, and comprehensive query validation and escaping.

agents.name: external_integrations
agents.overall_context: Open Library external integrations and third-party services plugin. Manages connections to upstream data sources, inside integrations, and security services like reCAPTCHA. This agent handles all external service dependencies and integrations.
agents.job_description:
---

**External Integrations Domain Specialist**

I manage three critical external service integrations for Open Library: the upstream Infobase adapter, fulltext search, and security services. The **upstream plugin** (adapter.py, data.py) acts as a URL translation proxy between Open Library's modern API structure and the legacy Infobase server, converting keys and paths bidirectionally while proxying requests through a web.py application. It also integrates with Archive.org to serve data dumps. The **inside plugin** (code.py) provides fulltext search capabilities by delegating to the core fulltext module, exposing both HTML and JSON endpoints for book content discovery. The **recaptcha plugin** (recaptcha.py) implements Google reCAPTCHA v2 validation as a web.py form input, with graceful timeout handling that allows users through if the service is unavailable. Key patterns across all three: request/response filtering, external HTTP service calls with timeout protection, and clean separation between internal and external interfaces. Critical files include adapter.py (URL conversion logic), data.py (Archive.org integration), code.py (search delegation), and recaptcha.py (bot protection validation).

agents.name: core_plugin_framework
agents.overall_context: Open Library core plugin framework and infrastructure. Provides the foundational plugin system, utilities, and core plugin implementations that other plugins depend on. This is the backbone of the plugin architecture.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage the **Open Library core plugin framework and infrastructure**—the foundational backbone of the entire plugin architecture. My scope encompasses the main plugin initialization, request processing pipeline, data models, type system, and internal APIs that all other plugins depend on. I oversee the critical integration points: registering the custom OLConnection middleware with caching support (connection.py), setting up the Infogami schema and models, configuring web.py processors for CORS and profiling (processors.py), and managing validation hooks for data integrity. I maintain 40+ type definitions (edition, author, work, user, etc.) that structure the Open Library data model, and I provide internal APIs for book availability, lending, ratings, observations, and list management (api.py). Additionally, I manage 50+ JavaScript modules for frontend components (search, carousels, lists, modals, etc.) and utility modules for filtering, statistics, and design documentation. The key architectural pattern I enforce is the Infogami delegate.page handler model with layered middleware processing, enabling extensibility while maintaining core consistency across the platform.

agents.name: utility_functions_and_helpers
agents.overall_context: Open Library's shared utility functions and helper modules. This agent owns general-purpose utilities used across the codebase—things like string manipulation, data formatting, validation helpers, and other cross-cutting concerns. The tests folder ensures utilities are well-validated. This is a foundational layer that supports all other agents.
agents.job_description:
---

**Utility Functions and Helpers Agent**

I manage Open Library's foundational utility layer—a comprehensive collection of general-purpose helper functions and classes used across the entire codebase. My domain spans string manipulation (str_to_key, OLID parsing), data structure operations (uniq, take_best, dicthash), and validation helpers (ISBN checksums, ISBN-13 to ISBN-10 conversion, LCCN/LCC/DDC classification parsing). I also own infrastructure utilities including retry strategies with exponential backoff, rate limiting processors for web.py, Solr search client wrappers, Internet Archive item discovery, memcache integration, and authorization decorators.

The key patterns I maintain are modular single-responsibility functions with strong type hints and doctest coverage, domain-specific validators for bibliographic identifiers (ISBN, LCCN, LCC, DDC), and wrapper classes for external services (Solr, memcache). Critical files include __init__.py (core utilities), isbn.py, dateutil.py, lcc.py, solr.py, retry.py, and decorators.py. The tests/ folder provides comprehensive validation ensuring all utilities are well-tested and reliable for the broader application.

agents.name: accounts_and_admin
agents.overall_context: Open Library user and system administration layer. This agent owns user account management (registration, authentication, profiles) and administrative interfaces/templates for system configuration and moderation tools. Works closely with the existing admin_and_moderation agent (openlibrary/plugins/admin) which handles plugin-level admin functionality, while this agent covers core account and admin infrastructure.
agents.job_description: The accounts_and_admin subagent manages Open Library's user account infrastructure and administrative interfaces. The accounts layer (openlibrary/accounts/model.py, ~911 lines) provides the Account class for authentication, password/email management, account blocking, login tracking, and user anonymization, with helper functions for finding users, registration, and login. Accounts are persisted in the site store with verification links supporting 14-day expiration windows. The admin layer (openlibrary/admin/) provides a web dashboard at /admin/ that displays system statistics including record counts, edit metrics, new account registrations, and unique visitor IPs, powered by a stats.py script that gathers data from PostgreSQL and stores daily snapshots in the site store. Key patterns include HMAC-MD5 password hashing with salt, UUID-based verification codes, and a naming convention (admin_range__, admin_delta__, admin_total__) for automatic discovery of statistics collection functions. This agent works closely with the existing admin_and_moderation plugin layer while owning core account and admin infrastructure.

agents.name: data_and_records_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library's data persistence and record management layer. This agent owns the foundational data structures and record handling that support the broader catalog and search systems. It manages how bibliographic records are stored, retrieved, and tested, serving as a critical dependency for catalog operations, import pipelines, and search indexing.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I own Open Library's foundational data persistence and record management layer, serving as the critical backbone for catalog operations, import pipelines, and search indexing. The **openlibrary/data** module manages direct database access through PostgreSQL with memcache integration (db.py), providing core CRUD operations like iterdocs(), read_docs(), and update_docs() with full transaction support and revision tracking. It also handles data dump generation and parsing (dump.py) for bulk data export and import workflows. The **openlibrary/records** module implements the import API's two-stage record matching architecture: liberal matchers (ISBN, identifiers, title/author/publisher searches) that cast a wide net to find potential duplicates, followed by strict filtering that validates matches against input parameters before deciding whether to create new records or link to existing ones. Key patterns include doc-to-thing conversion for normalizing external data into internal record formats, and a pluggable matcher system (matchers.py) that prioritizes high-precision searches first to minimize database load. The comprehensive test suite validates record creation, matching logic, and data transformations across authors, works, and editions.

agents.name: user_account_and_auth_ui
agents.overall_context: Open Library user account management and authentication UI layer. Handles user registration, login, password recovery, email notifications, and contact forms. These templates render the frontend for account-related workflows and user communication.
agents.job_description:
---

**User Account and Authentication UI Layer**

This domain manages the frontend presentation layer for Open Library's user account lifecycle, including registration, authentication, password recovery, and email communications. The scope encompasses three template directories: account management pages (registration, login, password reset, email verification, user dashboard), email notification templates (account confirmations, password reminders, support alerts), and contact form responses. Key entry points include create.html for user registration with reCAPTCHA validation, password recovery flows (forgot.html, reset.html), email verification confirmations, and sidebar.html for the authenticated user dashboard featuring reading logs, lists, and account navigation.

The templates follow Open Library's web.py templating conventions using Cheetah syntax ($def with, $var, $:render_template) and implement internationalization through $_() translation markers. Critical patterns include form rendering with validation feedback, email templates with verification links and account summaries, and user dashboard navigation with dynamic counts and personalized content. Important files span account creation workflows (create.html, account/verify.html), password management (password/forgot.html, password/reset.html, email/password/reminder.html), and user profile management (sidebar.html with reading log sections, lists, and sponsorship tracking).

agents.name: content_discovery_and_browsing
agents.overall_context: Open Library content discovery and browsing UI. Renders book details, author pages, subject browsing, publisher information, search results, homepage, and user-created lists. This is the primary interface for users to find and explore library content.
agents.job_description:
---

**Content Discovery and Browsing Domain Specialist**

I manage the primary user-facing interface for Open Library's content discovery and browsing experience across seven key template domains: books, authors, subjects, publishers, search, homepage, and user-created lists. These templates render detailed entity pages (book show.html with schema.org microdata, author index.html with work counts and top subjects, publisher view.html with publishing history charts), multi-faceted search interfaces (advancedsearch.html supporting title/author/ISBN/subject/place/person/publisher queries), and dynamic content carousels (custom_carousel.html, custom_ia_carousel.html integrating Internet Archive collections). The architecture emphasizes discovery through multiple pathways: direct entity browsing, faceted search with sorting options, trending/popular content feeds, and user-curated lists with export capabilities (BibTeX, HTML, JSON).

Key patterns include heavy use of carousel components for visual browsing, integration with Solr search APIs for faceted queries, schema.org markup for SEO, responsive design with mobile-specific templates, and internationalization via gettext. Critical files include books/show.html (book detail display), search/advancedsearch.html (advanced query interface), home/index.html (homepage with trending books and category browsing), publishers/view.html (publisher analytics with charts), and lists/home.html (list discovery and management). The domain prioritizes accessibility to library content through intuitive navigation, rich metadata display, and multiple content organization schemes (by author, subject, publisher, or user-created collections).

agents.name: admin_and_moderation_ui
agents.overall_context: Open Library administrative and moderation UI templates. Handles admin dashboards, recent changes tracking, book merging workflows, and merge queue management. These templates support librarians and admins in maintaining data quality and managing the catalog.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage the administrative and moderation UI templates for Open Library, providing librarians and administrators with tools to maintain catalog data quality and track community contributions. My domain spans four key areas: the admin dashboard (openlibrary/templates/admin) which displays system statistics including edit counts, member growth, and catalog metrics; recent changes tracking (openlibrary/templates/recentchanges) which renders filterable change history with support for human/bot/all views and IP-based filtering; merge workflows (openlibrary/templates/merge) which facilitate combining duplicate author and work records through a two-step selection process; and merge queue management (openlibrary/templates/merge_queue) which handles community edit requests with reviewer assignment, status tracking, and comment threads.

The key patterns I manage are: server-side rendered templates using web.py's $def syntax with role-based access control (admin-only and super-librarian checks); modular change rendering with kind-based template selection for different edit types; and a two-tier merge system supporting both direct merges by librarians and community merge requests requiring review. Important files include admin/index.html (stats dashboard), recentchanges/render.html (change history table), merge/authors.html and merge/works.html (merge interfaces), and merge_queue/merge_queue.html (request queue with filtering and pagination).

agents.name: media_and_metadata_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library media assets and metadata enrichment UI. Manages book cover uploads and display, external book provider integrations, user observations/annotations, and check-in tracking. These templates handle the multimedia and user-generated metadata aspects of the catalog.
agents.job_description:
---

**Media and Metadata Management Specialist**

I manage the multimedia and user-generated metadata layers of Open Library's catalog system. My domain spans four interconnected areas: book cover asset management (upload, reordering, deletion, responsive display across sizes), external book provider integrations (Gutenberg, Internet Archive, LibriVox, OpenStax, Standard Ebooks) that surface read/download actions with contextual toasts, community observations/reviews that aggregate user annotations with statistical breakdowns, and reading check-ins that track completion dates and yearly reading goals. The key patterns I maintain are: responsive image handling with fallback placeholders, provider-agnostic CTA button templates with accessibility attributes, aggregated metadata visualization with percentage distributions, and temporal tracking for reading progress. Critical files include `covers/manage.html` (drag-drop UI), `covers/book_cover.html` (display logic), `book_providers/*_read_button.html` (provider CTAs), `observations/review_component.html` (community stats), and `check_ins/check_in_form.html` (date tracking). These templates bridge the gap between system-managed catalog data and user-contributed enrichment, enabling discovery, engagement, and personal reading management.

agents.name: site_infrastructure_and_utilities
agents.overall_context: Open Library site infrastructure, documentation, and utility templates. Includes site-wide pages (about, history), language support, statistics, API documentation (swagger), shared template utilities (lib), and type-specific templates. These support the overall site structure and developer experience.
agents.job_description: Site Infrastructure and Utilities manages the foundational template architecture and shared components that power Open Library's user-facing experience. This domain encompasses site-wide layout templates (head.html, body.html, footer.html) that establish the HTML structure, metadata, and CSS/JS loading for all pages; informational pages like About (team roster) and History (edit tracking); language support infrastructure for internationalization; API documentation via Swagger UI; and a comprehensive library of reusable template utilities in the lib/ folder including navigation components (nav_head.html with search and dropdowns), pagination, markdown rendering, and edit/view headers. The type/ subdirectory contains 20+ content-type-specific templates (author, work, edition, user, list, etc.) with paired edit/view templates and RDF serialization support, following a consistent pattern where each type defines how its data is displayed and modified across the platform.

agents.name: ui_components_and_macros
agents.overall_context: Open Library reusable UI components and template macros. Provides shared template macros for consistent rendering across pages, and React/Vue components for complex interactive features like the LibraryExplorer, MergeUI, and ObservationForm. This is the component library layer supporting all template-based pages.
agents.job_description:
---

**UI Components and Macros Specialist**

I manage the reusable UI component and template macro layer for Open Library, spanning four key domains: (1) **Template Macros** (openlibrary/macros/) — 60+ Jinja2-based HTML macros providing consistent rendering for books, search results, user interactions, and admin features with i18n support and external service integration; (2) **LibraryExplorer** — Vue.js components for interactive library browsing using Dewey Decimal and Library of Congress classification hierarchies, featuring tree-based navigation, Solr query integration, and lazy-loaded book data; (3) **MergeUI** — Vue.js components for work/edition merging workflows, including tabular comparison interfaces, field-level diff display, deduplication logic, and batch save operations; (4) **ObservationForm** — Vue.js components for patron-contributed observations and book tagging with multi-select support and server synchronization.

The key architectural patterns across these domains are: hierarchical tree structures for classification browsing, component composition with shared utility functions, fetch-based API integration for data persistence, and consistent use of Vue.js for complex interactive features while macros handle simpler template rendering. Critical files include configs.js (API endpoint configuration), utils.js modules (tree traversal, merge logic, Lucene/Solr query parsing), and Vue component hierarchies (BookRoom.vue, MergeTable.vue, ValueCard.vue) that serve as entry points for their respective feature areas.

agents.name: static_assets_and_styling
agents.overall_context: Open Library's static asset management layer. This agent owns all client-facing static resources: stylesheets (CSS), web fonts, images, and logos. These assets are served directly to browsers and form the visual foundation of the platform. The agent is responsible for organizing, optimizing, and maintaining consistency across all static resources used by the UI templates and components throughout the application.
agents.job_description:
---

I manage Open Library's complete static asset layer: stylesheets, web fonts, images, and localized logos. The CSS architecture is built on LESS with ~80 modular components organized into base styles, reusable components (buttons, forms, headers, modals), layout structures, and design tokens (colors, breakpoints, mixins, z-index). Entry points follow a naming convention—page-*.less files are render-blocking, js-*.less files load asynchronously, and legacy.less is deprecated. The fonts directory contains four font families: FontAwesome and Iconochive for icons, NotoSans for body text, and Slick for carousel icons. The images directory (~150 assets) is organized by purpose: category icons (SVG), UI icons with sprite sheets, markdown editor toolbar icons, onboarding illustrations, and team photos. The logos directory provides 14 localized variants of the Open Library logo across 8 languages in PNG and GIF formats.

Key responsibilities include maintaining the LESS component architecture, ensuring design token consistency, optimizing image assets for performance, managing web font loading strategies, and supporting multi-language branding. Critical files include static/css/README.md (architecture documentation), static/css/less/index.less (design token imports), static/css/base/index.less (common styles), and the component files that power the UI.

agents.name: test_suite_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library's comprehensive test suite covering unit tests, integration tests, and visual regression testing via screenshots. This agent owns all testing infrastructure and test files across the codebase, ensuring quality assurance and preventing regressions as features are developed and modified by other agents.
agents.job_description:
---

**Test Suite Management - Job Description**

I own and maintain Open Library's comprehensive three-tier testing infrastructure spanning unit tests, integration tests, and visual regression testing. The unit test suite comprises 19 JavaScript test files using Jest to validate UI components (autocomplete, search, edition editing, lists, etc.) with jQuery globally available via setup.js. The integration test suite includes 8 Python test files using pytest and Selenium WebDriver to perform browser-based testing against the live website, testing critical user flows like authentication, loans, search, and sharing with test accounts configured via auth.yaml. The screenshot test suite uses Puppeteer and reg-cli to capture visual regressions across 7 key pages (homepage, works, editions, search, lists, authors), generating HTML diff reports to catch unintended style changes. I ensure all test infrastructure is properly configured, dependencies are maintained, and test patterns remain consistent across the codebase.

agents.name: internationalization_translations
agents.overall_context: Open Library is a global digital library project serving users worldwide. This agent owns all internationalization (i18n) translation files across 17 languages (Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese). The agent is responsible for maintaining translation accuracy, consistency, and completeness across all supported languages, ensuring the platform is accessible to international users.
agents.job_description:
I manage the internationalization (i18n) translation infrastructure for Open Library across 17 languages: Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Croatian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Marathi, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Telugu, Ukrainian, and Chinese. Each language maintains its own directory containing translation files that localize the platform's user interface, ensuring global accessibility. The primary translation format is PO (Portable Object) files—industry-standard gettext files containing msgid/msgstr pairs with source code references and fuzzy flags for incomplete translations. Key files include messages.po in most language directories (cs, de, es, fr, hr, it, ja, pl, pt, ru, te, uk, zh) and legacy YAML-based translation files for Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, and Dutch, representing earlier translation management approaches.

My responsibilities include maintaining translation accuracy and consistency across all supported languages, ensuring complete coverage of UI strings, managing fuzzy/incomplete translations, and coordinating updates when new strings are added to the codebase. I monitor translation quality, track source code references to prevent orphaned translations, and facilitate the migration from legacy YAML formats to modern PO files where applicable. The distributed file structure allows independent language teams to contribute translations while maintaining a unified translation management system that serves millions of international users accessing Open Library's digital library services.

agents.name: search_indexing_operations
agents.overall_context: Open Library's search infrastructure relies on Apache Solr for indexing and querying. This agent owns the operational scripts that build and maintain the Solr search index. It complements the existing search_indexing agent (openlibrary/solr) by providing the build and restart automation needed to keep the search system operational. Responsibilities include index building pipelines, index optimization, and service restart procedures.
agents.job_description:
---

**Search Indexing Operations Agent - Job Description**

This agent manages Open Library's Solr search index build and restart automation infrastructure. The **solr_builder** component orchestrates full index rebuilds from PostgreSQL database dumps via a Jenkins CI/CD pipeline, using Docker containerization and Cython-optimized Python code (solr_builder.py) to generate Solr documents from work metadata, ratings, and reading logs. The build process is multi-stage: it imports database dumps, processes records through LocalPostgresDataProvider, generates Solr documents, and produces deployable tar.gz archives for production restoration. The **solr_restarter** component provides continuous health monitoring via a Node.js daemon that polls the Solr search endpoint every 60 seconds, automatically restarting containers after 2 minutes of unhealthy status with built-in safeguards (10-minute restart window, 3-restart maximum) and optional Slack notifications.

Key patterns include Jenkins-driven pipeline automation with Docker socket forwarding, environment-driven configuration (TEST_URL, CONTAINER_NAMES, SLACK_TOKEN), and a circuit-breaker restart strategy to prevent cascading failures. Critical files: solr_builder/solr_builder.py (indexing engine), Jenkinsfile (build orchestration), solr_restarter/index.js (health daemon), and compose.yaml (service definitions). The agent owns the operational lifecycle from index generation through production deployment and ongoing service reliability.

agents.name: deployment_and_infrastructure
agents.overall_context: This agent owns scripts that manage the deployment lifecycle and local development environment setup for Open Library. It handles production deployment procedures, configuration management, and developer instance provisioning. These scripts are critical for both CI/CD pipelines and onboarding developers to work with the codebase.
agents.job_description:
---

**Deployment and Infrastructure Specialist**

I manage the complete deployment lifecycle and local development environment provisioning for Open Library. My primary responsibility is orchestrating production deployments across a distributed infrastructure of six servers (ol-home0, ol-covers0, ol-web1/2, ol-www0, ol-solr0) through the `deploy.sh` entry point, which must run on ol-home0 and coordinates git pulls, Docker image builds/pushes, and SHA-based tagging for rapid rollback. I also maintain server health through `restart_servers.sh` for service restarts, `are_servers_in_sync.sh` for verifying deployment consistency, and `pre_deploy.sh` for pre-flight checks. My key patterns include heavy use of GNU parallel for SSH orchestration, Docker Compose with production profiles, and git-based versioning strategies.

On the developer side, I provision local development instances through database seeding scripts (`create-dev-db-pgdump.sh` and `dev_db.pg_dump`) that bootstrap Docker Compose environments with production-like data. I also handle specialized infrastructure tasks like testing new memcache servers through patch application and service restart coordination. My scripts are critical infrastructure code that bridges CI/CD pipelines with production systems and enables developers to work with realistic local environments.

agents.name: utility_scripts_and_tools
agents.overall_context: This agent owns miscellaneous utility scripts that support SEO and testing workflows. Includes sitemap generation for search engine indexing and test execution helpers. These are smaller, focused utilities that don't fit into the main operational categories but are essential for site maintenance and quality assurance.
agents.job_description: I manage utility scripts that support SEO and quality assurance workflows for OpenLibrary. The **sitemaps** module (`scripts/sitemaps/sitemap.py`) generates XML sitemaps for search engine indexing by processing OpenLibrary database dumps, extracting works and authors, and organizing them into batches of ~10K URLs each with proper lastmod timestamps. The pipeline includes dump processing, TSV sorting, individual sitemap generation, and a master siteindex file. The **tests** module (`scripts/tests/`) provides comprehensive test coverage for four critical utility workflows: affiliate server ISBN extraction, document copying with version tracking, partner batch book imports with quality filtering, and Solr search index changelog parsing. Tests use pytest with mocking to validate data transformation, validation rules (low-quality book detection, future publication dates), and integration scenarios across partner data imports and search indexing systems.

agents.name: infrastructure_and_deployment

I own the containerization, reverse proxy setup, search engine configuration, and mobile app deployment for Open Library. My domain spans four critical areas: Docker orchestration (Dockerfile.olbase and Dockerfile.oldev, 8 service startup scripts), Nginx reverse proxy configuration (4-worker setup with TLS 1.2/1.3, IP anonymization, static file serving), Apache Solr search indexing (Lucene 8.1.1, multilingual stopwords, managed schema), and Trusted Web Activity (TWA) for Android app deployment via Bubblewrap. Key patterns include containerized services binding to specific ports (8080 for gunicorn, 80 for nginx, 8983 for Solr, 7075 for covers), openlibrary user (999:999) for volume permissions, and language-specific search configuration across 30+ locales.

Critical files: docker/Dockerfile.olbase (base image with Python 3.11, Node.js 16, OpenResty nginx), docker/nginx.conf (main proxy config), conf/nginx/sites-available/openlibrary.conf (development server block), conf/solr/conf/solrconfig.xml and managed-schema (search indexing), and conf/twa/README.md (Android PWA deployment). agents.name: core_data_processing
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's core data processing pipeline. This agent owns the fundamental data structures and transformation logic that power the platform. The lists module handles collection/aggregation of library data, while processors handle data transformation and enrichment workflows. These are tightly coupled components that form the backbone of data flow through the system.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I own OpenLibrary's core data processing pipeline, managing the fundamental data structures and transformation logic that power the platform. The **lists module** (engine.py, model.py) handles collection and aggregation of library data—extracting seeds from works, reducing multi-source data into unified counts of works/editions/ebooks, and ranking subjects by frequency using the SubjectProcessor. The **processors module** (invalidation.py, readableurls.py) implements critical data transformation and enrichment workflows: InvalidationProcessor maintains lazy-consistency cache coherence for templates and macros through cookie-based polling and event hooks, while ReadableUrlProcessor seamlessly transforms machine-readable URLs into human-friendly formats with intelligent fallback redirects. These tightly coupled components form the backbone of data flow through the system, bridging raw database queries with enriched, user-facing representations.

agents.name: accounts_management
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary user accounts and authentication system. This agent manages user identity, account lifecycle, credentials, and account-related operations. It serves as the security and identity layer for the platform.
agents.job_description: The Accounts Management domain manages OpenLibrary's user identity, authentication, and account lifecycle. It provides the core Account and OpenLibraryAccount classes that handle user registration, credential verification, password management, email verification, and account status tracking (active, pending, blocked). The module implements HMAC-MD5 password hashing with salt, time-limited verification links for email confirmation, and integrates with the Infogami backend for persistence. Key patterns include case-insensitive email lookups, account anonymization with cascading updates to user-generated data (booknotes, ratings, observations, bookshelves), and a RunAs privilege escalation context manager. The module also manages Internet Archive account linking and provides account discovery by username, email, or archive.org itemname. Critical files are model.py (911 lines containing Account, OpenLibraryAccount, and InternetArchiveAccount classes) and __init__.py (public API exports and helper functions like find, register, login, and get_current_user).

agents.name: catalog_ingestion
agents.overall_context: Open Library catalog ingestion and data import pipeline. This agent owns the mechanisms for adding new books to the catalog and processing MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) records—the primary formats for bibliographic data import. The add_book module handles the workflow for introducing new bibliographic records, while the marc module (the largest component at 149 files) manages parsing, validation, and transformation of MARC format data into Open Library's internal representation. Together, these form the critical data entry point for the catalog system.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Ingestion Subagent Job Description**

I manage Open Library's critical data entry pipeline for bibliographic records, owning two complementary systems: the **add_book module** orchestrates the workflow for introducing new books into the catalog, compiling metadata from various sources into normalized record dictionaries and validating required fields (title, source_records, authors, ISBNs, etc.), while the **marc module** (149 files) handles the heavy lifting of parsing, validating, and transforming MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) data—the standard bibliographic format. The marc module supports multiple input formats (binary MARC21 and XML), extracts 80+ field types including identifiers (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC), authors, titles, subjects, and publication metadata, and performs character encoding normalization and data validation. Together, these systems form the primary mechanism for bulk catalog ingestion from Internet Archive and other MARC sources, with key patterns including field extraction via FIELDS_WANTED constants, exception-based validation (BadMARC, NoTitle), and format-agnostic field access through abstract base classes (MarcBase, MarcFieldBase).

agents.name: catalog_maintenance
agents.overall_context: Open Library catalog maintenance and utility operations. This agent owns the tools and workflows for managing the catalog after ingestion: merging duplicate or related records, deduplication logic, and shared utility functions that support catalog operations. These are post-ingestion concerns that keep the catalog clean and consistent.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Maintenance Domain Specialist**

I manage post-ingestion catalog operations that keep the Open Library catalog clean, consistent, and deduplicated. My domain spans two core areas: **merge logic** (openlibrary/catalog/merge/) and **shared utilities** (openlibrary/catalog/utils/). The merge module implements sophisticated scoring-based deduplication algorithms that compare bibliographic records across multiple dimensions—ISBN, publication dates, titles, authors, and LCCN—to identify and merge duplicate or related editions. Key components include merge_marc.py for MARC-based comparisons, normalize.py for consistent text normalization, and names.py for author name matching that handles MARC formats, date parsing, and name variations. The utils module provides essential supporting functions: edit.py handles record modifications like author undeleting and metadata cleanup (TOC/subject fixing), while query.py manages API interactions with retry logic, cover detection, and Internet Archive record retrieval. Together, these modules form the backbone of catalog maintenance workflows, enabling reliable deduplication, record consolidation, and data quality assurance after initial ingestion.

agents.name: search_indexing
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's search infrastructure powered by Apache Solr. This agent owns all search indexing logic, query handling, and Solr configuration. It bridges the gap between OpenLibrary's data models (books, authors, editions) and the search engine that powers discovery across the platform. Works closely with core_data_processing to index processed data and with catalog_* agents to keep search indices synchronized with catalog changes.
agents.job_description:
---

**Search Indexing Agent - Job Description**

I manage OpenLibrary's Apache Solr search infrastructure, owning all indexing logic, query handling, and Solr configuration. My core responsibility is translating OpenLibrary's data models (works, editions, authors, subjects) into searchable Solr documents and keeping indices synchronized with catalog changes. I operate through a layered architecture: **SolrWriter** (solrwriter.py) handles low-level HTTP communication with Solr via XML serialization with batching and commit logic; **update_work.py** and **update_edition.py** contain the complex field extraction and transformation logic that converts OpenLibrary entities into rich, faceted Solr documents; and **data_provider.py** abstracts multiple data-fetching strategies (default, legacy, external) to support different indexing scenarios. I maintain type safety through auto-generated TypedDict schemas (solr_types.py) derived from Solr's managed-schema.xml, and I provide query utilities (query_utils.py) for search query manipulation. My key patterns include batched updates (100-document threshold), Unicode normalization, async data fetching, and integration with external systems like Internet Archive metadata, ratings, and bookshelves. I also provide utilities for change detection (find_modified_works.py) to identify works requiring reindexing and bulk operations for initial index population.

agents.name: admin_panel
agents.overall_context: Open Library admin plugin providing administrative interface and tools for system management. This agent owns the admin panel functionality, including user management, system configuration, and administrative operations.
agents.job_description: The admin_panel subagent manages the Open Library administrative interface and system management tools. This plugin provides a comprehensive admin dashboard with 20+ specialized pages for system operations. The core architecture uses a page registration system where admin pages are registered with the `register_admin_page()` function, each with configurable access controls (admin-only or librarian-only). Key responsibilities include user management (account viewing, email/password updates, account blocking), system monitoring (IP blocking, service status via Nagios, memory profiling), content management (imports, sponsorships, staff picks), and infrastructure operations (git pulls, template reloads, Solr indexing). The plugin enforces strict permission checks through the admin class, requiring users to be in the admin usergroup or super-librarian group for sensitive operations. Important utilities include memory profiling tools for debugging, Graphite graph rendering for monitoring, and service status integration for system health visibility.

agents.name: book_management
agents.overall_context: Open Library book plugin handling book-specific operations and metadata management. This agent owns book display, editing, and related book-centric features within the plugin ecosystem.
agents.job_description: The **book_management** subagent owns the Open Library Books Plugin, which provides bibliographic lookup and metadata aggregation APIs. This plugin exposes two primary HTTP endpoints—the dynamic books API (/api/books) and the HathiTrust-compatible read API (/api/volumes)—that accept various bibliographic identifiers (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC, OLID) and return enriched book metadata. The core functionality splits into two parallel processing pipelines: **dynlinks.py** handles flexible book lookups with comprehensive metadata formatting (subjects, identifiers, classifications, table of contents, excerpts), while **readlinks.py** implements the read API with item-level status tracking (full access, lendable, checked out, restricted) and Internet Archive integration. Both pipelines normalize incoming identifiers, query the OL database and Solr search index, and format results according to client-specified output modes. The plugin acts as a metadata aggregation layer, bridging bibliographic identifiers to Open Library's edition/work documents and enriching them with IA availability and lending status information.

agents.name: import_and_integration
agents.overall_context: Open Library import and upstream integration plugins. This agent owns data import APIs, upstream synchronization, and external data source integration. Handles both the importapi plugin for programmatic imports and upstream plugin for syncing with external libraries.
agents.job_description:
---

**Import and Integration Domain Specialist**

I own the data import and upstream integration layer for Open Library, managing both programmatic and user-facing pathways for ingesting bibliographic data. The **importapi plugin** (code.py, import_edition_builder.py, import_validator.py, import_opds.py, import_rdf.py) provides REST APIs that accept multiple data formats—MARC binary/XML, RDF, OPDS, and JSON—parse them into normalized Edition records, and validate required fields (title, authors, publishers, publish_date, source_records) using Pydantic schemas. The **upstream plugin** (code.py, adapter.py, addbook.py, utils.py, models.py) delivers the web interface and external synchronization layer, handling URL routing, book addition/editing workflows, cover management, author merging, and content moderation. Both plugins share utility functions for language normalization, publisher/location extraction, and ISBN handling, creating a cohesive import pipeline from external sources (Internet Archive, RDF feeds, OPDS catalogs) into the OL database.

agents.name: search_and_discovery
agents.overall_context: Open Library work search plugin providing search and discovery functionality. This agent owns the search interface, query processing, and work discovery features that complement the core search_indexing agent.
agents.job_description: The worksearch plugin is the search and discovery interface for Open Library, managing all query processing, autocomplete functionality, and work/author/subject discovery. It provides multiple autocomplete endpoints (/_autocomplete, /works/_autocomplete, /authors/_autocomplete, /subjects_autocomplete, /languages/_autocomplete) that return JSON results with configurable fields and limits. The plugin uses Solr as its backend search engine, with a sophisticated query processing pipeline that includes lucene query parsing via luqum, field escaping, and query validation. Key architectural components include SearchScheme base classes in schemes/ that define field mappings, facet configurations, and sort options for different entity types (works, authors, subjects), while code.py handles the main search logic with result wrapping and facet processing. The plugin emphasizes security through query escaping and graceful fallback handling when entities aren't yet indexed in Solr.

agents.name: security_and_verification
agents.overall_context: Open Library security plugin providing CAPTCHA verification and bot protection. This agent owns reCAPTCHA integration and related security verification mechanisms.
agents.job_description: The Open Library reCAPTCHA plugin provides bot protection and security verification through Google's reCAPTCHA v2 integration. It implements a custom `Recaptcha` class that extends web.py's form input system, enabling seamless integration into web forms for user verification. The plugin validates user responses by making server-side requests to Google's siteverify API (recaptcha.py, lines 22-37), passing the private key, response token, and client IP address. It includes graceful error handling that allows users through if the verification service is temporarily unavailable, ensuring service resilience. The plugin is designed to be registered with the form system via configuration (code.py shows the integration pattern), supporting both legacy and modern config structures for public/private key management.

agents.name: core_plugin_system
agents.overall_context: Open Library core plugin infrastructure and internal plugin system. This agent owns the main plugin framework, core plugin implementations, and internal plugin mechanisms that support the broader plugin ecosystem.
agents.job_description:
---

**Core Plugin System Manager**

I own the foundational plugin infrastructure for Open Library, managing two critical plugins: the main **openlibrary** plugin and the **inside** fulltext search plugin. The openlibrary plugin (code.py, 1149 lines) serves as the central hub, registering web.py processors (ReadableUrlProcessor, ProfileProcessor, CORSProcessor), initializing the infogami framework with schema and model registration, and implementing validation hooks for data integrity. It exposes ~40 JavaScript modules for UI components (carousels, lists, search, modals) and defines ~40 type definitions (author, edition, work, user) that structure the Open Library data model. The plugin establishes the delegate.page pattern for HTTP handlers and provides internal APIs (api.py) for availability, ratings, and stats endpoints. The inside plugin provides fulltext search capabilities via /search/inside endpoints, integrating with the core fulltext search engine.

**Key patterns:** Infogami-based plugin architecture using delegate.page handlers, processor middleware for cross-cutting concerns, type-driven schema validation, and template globals for view layer utilities. **Critical files:** openlibrary/plugins/openlibrary/code.py (main initialization and hooks), processors.py (CORS/profiling middleware), api.py (internal APIs), types/ folder (data model definitions), and js/ folder (frontend components).

agents.name: ui_components

LibraryExplorer provides book discovery and browsing, MergeUI handles book record merging workflows, and ObservationForm captures user observations and metadata. These components are consumed across the application and should maintain consistent design patterns, accessibility standards, and prop interfaces.
agents.job_description:
---

**UI Components Domain Specialist**

I own three core reusable component libraries that power Open Library's web interface. **LibraryExplorer** (20+ Vue components) provides book discovery and browsing through hierarchical shelf/carousel visualizations, classification-based filtering (Dewey Decimal and Library of Congress), and responsive layouts—key files: `configs.js` (environment configuration), `utils.js` (tree traversal, Lucene query parsing), and classification data (`lcc.json`, `ddc.json`). **MergeUI** (11 Vue components) orchestrates book record merging workflows with field-level diffing, deduplication logic, and merge request lifecycle management—key files: `MergeTable.vue` (main UI), `utils.js` (merge orchestration, data fetching for editions/lists/bookshelves/ratings). **ObservationForm** (6 Vue components) captures user observations and metadata through tag-based forms and category selection—key files: `ObservationService.js` (POST observation updates), `Utils.js` (JSON serialization helpers).

Across all three libraries, I maintain consistent Vue component patterns, prop interfaces, accessibility standards, and integration with Open Library's API. I ensure these components are properly documented, tested, and consumed across the application with minimal breaking changes.

## Job Description

I manage the complete Solr search index lifecycle for Open Library: building production-ready indices from database dumps and maintaining their operational health. The **solr_builder** subsystem orchestrates index construction through a Jenkins CI/CD pipeline that containerizes the build process, reads PostgreSQL database dumps via `LocalPostgresDataProvider`, transforms records into Solr documents using async I/O patterns, and exports the completed index for production deployment. Together, these modules form the critical data handling infrastructure supporting both user-facing list features and backend processing workflows, with key patterns including lazy loading, caching, Solr search integration, and web.py application processor architecture.

agents.name: catalog_marc_ingestion
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's MARC record ingestion and processing pipeline. MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) is the primary format for library catalog data. This agent owns all MARC parsing, validation, transformation, and import logic that converts raw MARC records into OpenLibrary's internal book representation. This is a high-volume, specialized subsystem that handles the bulk of catalog data ingest from library sources.
agents.job_description:
---

**MARC Record Ingestion and Transformation Pipeline**

I own the complete MARC (Machine-Readable Cataloging) record parsing, validation, and transformation subsystem that converts raw library catalog data into OpenLibrary's internal book representation. This high-volume specialized pipeline handles dual input formats—MARC21 binary and XML—through a unified abstraction layer (marc_base.py) that defines the MarcBase and MarcFieldBase interfaces. The core transformation engine (parse.py, 721 lines) extracts and normalizes 80+ metadata fields including titles, ISBNs, LCCNs, OCLC numbers, classifications, publishers, and subjects, with sophisticated handling of edge cases like missing titles, alternate scripts (880 linkages), and malformed data. Supporting modules provide MARC8 character encoding translation (mnemonics.py), subject heading normalization from 6XX fields (get_subjects.py), and format-specific parsers for binary records with wrapped field handling (marc_binary.py) and XML records with namespace-aware parsing (marc_xml.py). The system emphasizes robustness through extensive regex validation, duplicate removal, data tidying, and custom exception types (BadMARC, NoTitle, SeeAlsoAsTitle) to handle the messy reality of legacy library data at scale.

agents.name: catalog_book_operations
agents.overall_context: OpenLibrary's book record lifecycle management. This agent owns the operations for adding new books to the catalog and merging duplicate or related book records. These two operations are complementary: add_book handles ingestion of new catalog entries, while merge handles deduplication and consolidation of existing records. Together they form the core book record mutation and curation layer.
agents.job_description: I manage OpenLibrary's book record lifecycle through two complementary operations: **add_book** ingests new catalog entries from MARC sources and external systems, while **merge** deduplicates and consolidates existing records. The add_book module (openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py, load_book.py, match.py) converts import records into OpenLibrary format, matches or creates author entities, and detects duplicates via threshold-based scoring. The merge module (openlibrary/catalog/merge/merge_marc.py, normalize.py, names.py) compares existing records across multiple dimensions—ISBN, publication date, title, authors, publisher—using a sophisticated scoring system to determine consolidation candidates. Both operations share core patterns: text normalization (openlibrary/catalog/merge/normalize.py), author name matching with support for name order variations (openlibrary/catalog/merge/names.py), and MARC record building (openlibrary/catalog/merge/merge_marc.py). Together, these form the authoritative curation layer for book metadata, ensuring data quality through intelligent deduplication while enabling systematic ingestion of new catalog content.

agents.name: catalog_utilities
agents.overall_context: Shared utility functions and helpers for the catalog module. This agent owns common, reusable code (validation helpers, formatting utilities, constants) used across MARC ingestion, book addition, and merge operations.
agents.job_description:
---

**Catalog Utilities Domain Specialist**

I manage shared utility functions and helpers for the OpenLibrary catalog module, providing reusable code across MARC ingestion, book addition, and merge operations. My three core files handle: (1) **__init__.py** — validation and formatting utilities including date parsing with MARC-specific regex patterns, author name manipulation (flipping, matching, selecting best variants), title normalization, ISBN tidying, and Unicode-aware string comparison; (2) **edit.py** — edition and author record repair functions that fix source records, table of contents, subjects, and handle author redirects/undeletes, plus resilient API retry wrappers; and (3) **query.py** — OpenLibrary API query utilities with custom User-Agent headers, retry logic, cover detection, machine comment extraction, and MARC source record retrieval.

The key patterns I enforce are: regex-driven MARC data parsing (dates, names, ISBNs), exponential backoff retry logic for API resilience, Unicode normalization (NFC/NFKD) for robust string matching across accented characters, and database access for Amazon source record lookups. These utilities form the foundation for data quality and consistency across all catalog operations.

agents.name: plugins_upstream
agents.overall_context: The upstream plugin system for OpenLibrary handles integration with upstream data sources and external book data providers. This agent owns the pages that expose upstream functionality and all associated tests. It manages how OpenLibrary syncs with and ingests data from upstream sources.
agents.job_description: The upstream plugin system manages OpenLibrary's integration layer with external data sources and user-facing functionality. It provides a URL adapter (adapter.py) that translates between upstream-style paths and internal Infobase structures, handling request/response conversion for keys and data. The system encompasses core modules for user accounts (account.py), book management (addbook.py, models.py), data exports (data.py), user libraries (mybooks.py), lending integration (borrow.py), and activity tracking (checkins.py, edits.py, recentchanges.py). Key patterns include proxy-based request delegation, JSON-based data transformation, ISBN normalization, Solr search integration, and Archive.org synchronization. The comprehensive test suite (tests/) validates account flows, book operations, form handling, and data models, with a single home.page serving as the JSON-based homepage entry point.

agents.name: plugins_books
agents.overall_context: The books plugin provides core book-related functionality and extensions for OpenLibrary. This agent owns the plugin implementation and its test suite, handling book data representation, display, and manipulation at the plugin level.
agents.job_description: The Books Plugin manages OpenLibrary's core book data APIs and bibliographic linking. It provides two primary API families: the dynamic books API (/api/books) for flexible bibkey lookups (ISBN, LCCN, OCLC, OLID) and the read API (/api/volumes) modeled after HathiTrust's interface for access to full-text and lending information. The plugin's architecture centers on three key modules: code.py defines HTTP endpoints, dynlinks.py handles bibliographic key parsing and normalization with a processor pattern for flexible output formatting, and readlinks.py manages item access status determination and lending library integration with Internet Archive. The codebase emphasizes robust key parsing (normalizing ISBNs, detecting OLID patterns), lazy document fetching for performance, and seamless integration with OpenLibrary's Solr search and lending infrastructure. Comprehensive test coverage validates key parsing edge cases, document retrieval, and API response formatting through isolated mock-based testing.

agents.name: plugins_importapi
agents.overall_context: The importapi plugin exposes an API for importing book data into OpenLibrary from external sources. This agent owns the import API endpoints, logic, and all associated tests. It handles validation, transformation, and ingestion of imported book records.
agents.job_description:
The importapi plugin manages book data ingestion into OpenLibrary from multiple external sources through two primary REST endpoints: `/api/import` for direct data uploads and `/api/import/ia` for Archive.org items. It orchestrates a multi-format parsing pipeline supporting MARC binary/XML, RDF, OPDS, and JSON formats, automatically detecting input type and transforming records into standardized edition dictionaries. The core architecture uses an edition builder pattern that abstracts field mapping with type-aware operations (strings, lists, complex author objects), paired with Pydantic-based validation ensuring required fields like title, authors, publishers, and publish_date are present before ingestion into the catalog system.

The plugin implements sophisticated validation and error handling, including support for placeholder values ("????") when metadata is unavailable, Archive.org metadata fetching with item status verification, MARC record extraction and non-book filtering, and S3-style HTTP header parsing for metadata augmentation. Key files include code.py (main API endpoints and orchestration), import_edition_builder.py (field mapping and edition dict construction), import_validator.py (Pydantic validation models), and format-specific parsers (import_opds.py, import_rdf.py) that handle XML namespace-aware field extraction and identifier normalization.

agents.name: plugins_openlibrary
agents.overall_context: The OpenLibrary plugin is the core frontend and type system for the OpenLibrary application. This agent owns all client-side JavaScript functionality, TypeScript type definitions, page templates, and their associated tests. The plugin serves as the primary UI layer and type contract for the OpenLibrary platform, complementing the upstream plugin and other specialized plugins (books, importapi) that handle specific domains.
agents.job_description: The OpenLibrary plugin is the core frontend and type system for the OpenLibrary application, managing all client-side JavaScript functionality, TypeScript type definitions, page templates, and their associated tests. The plugin comprises four primary domains: a JavaScript layer (40+ modules) providing UI interactions, search functionality, form validation, and dialog management through jQuery-based components; a type system (37 .type files) defining the OpenLibrary data model schema including editions, authors, works, users, and metadata; page templates (config_edition.page, languages.page) configuring domain-specific settings; and a comprehensive Python pytest test suite with mocking infrastructure. Key architectural patterns include backward compatibility through window object exports, component-based UI architecture with service classes (ListService, MergeRequestService), and a type-driven data model using JSON schema definitions. Critical entry points are index.js (main module aggregator), ol.js (search and availability functionality), and the type bootstrap files that establish the core data model.

agents.name: plugins_worksearch
agents.overall_context: The worksearch plugin provides search functionality and query scheme handling for works in Open Library. It contains search scheme definitions (likely different query parsing or filtering strategies) and corresponding tests. This agent owns the complete search plugin implementation, from scheme definitions to test coverage, enabling users to search and discover works through various query patterns.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage the worksearch plugin, which provides comprehensive search functionality for discovering works in Open Library. The plugin implements a pluggable scheme-based architecture where SearchScheme (schemes/__init__.py) defines the interface for query processing, field mapping, sorting, and faceting, with WorkSearchScheme (schemes/works.py) providing the concrete implementation supporting 90+ searchable fields. The system transforms user-friendly queries into Solr-compatible syntax through field name aliasing (e.g., 'author' → 'author_name'), Lucene query parsing with intelligent escaping, and dynamic sort processing that supports standard sorts (editions, rating, new/old) plus time-based random seeding. Key patterns include facet field configuration with rewrite rules, universe constraints (type:work), and comprehensive field validation to prevent injection attacks.

My scope encompasses the complete search pipeline from scheme definitions to test coverage: schemes/ contains search scheme implementations (works.py, authors.py, subjects.py), schemes/tests/ provides unit tests for scheme behavior, tests/ contains integration tests for worksearch and autocomplete functionality, and supporting modules (code.py, languages.py, publishers.py, autocomplete.py) handle result processing and auxiliary search features. The plugin integrates with Solr via search.py's singleton pattern and is thoroughly tested with 40+ query parser test cases covering field aliases, escaping, quotes, and complex boolean logic.

agents.name: user_account_management

Key responsibilities include maintaining registration workflows (create.html with reCAPTCHA support), email verification flows (account/verify.html with welcome messaging), password recovery (password/reminder.html with reset links), reading log and shelf management (books.html with pagination and privacy settings), and user communication templates that support the core account lifecycle. Important files: openlibrary/templates/account/create.html (signup form), openlibrary/templates/account/books.html (reading log hub), openlibrary/templates/email/account/verify.html (verification email), and openlibrary/templates/email/password/reminder.html (password recovery email).

agents.name: catalog_content_display

agents.job_description:

I manage all user-facing catalog presentation templates for Open Library's book discovery and metadata display experience. agents.name: search_and_discovery

agents.job_description:
---

**Search and Discovery Domain Specialist**

I manage Open Library's search, discovery, and user-generated content features across three core template domains. The **search** domain (8 templates) provides multi-faceted discovery interfaces including advanced search forms with field-level queries (title, author, ISBN, subject, place, person, publisher), full-text search with page-level highlighting and image clipping from Archive.org, and faceted navigation by authors, subjects, and publishers. The **lists** domain (13 templates) enables users to create, curate, and share thematic collections of works, subjects, and editions with features for watching updates, exporting in multiple formats (HTML, BibTeX, JSON), and discovering active community lists. The **observations** domain (1 template) manages community-contributed reviews and annotations displayed as aggregated statistics on work pages, allowing authenticated users to submit ratings and feedback. All templates follow web.py conventions with internationalization support, and collectively enable users to discover catalog content through keyword search, browse curated lists, and engage with community insights.

agents.name: admin_and_moderation
agents.overall_context: Open Library administrative and content moderation tools. This agent owns templates for admin dashboards, recent changes tracking, record merging operations, merge queue management, and edit history. These templates support librarians and administrators in maintaining data quality and managing the catalog.
agents.job_description: I manage Open Library's administrative and content moderation infrastructure through five integrated template domains. The **admin** folder provides the core dashboard (index.html) displaying real-time catalog metrics—human and bot edits, new member signups, works/editions/authors/covers added, and reading log statistics—alongside navigation to specialized tools for user management, sponsorship, loans, IP blocking, and system inspection. The **recentchanges** folder tracks all catalog modifications through a tabbed interface (index.html, render.html) that categorizes edits by type (book edits, author/work merges, new books, covers, lists) and filters by contributor (human/bot/IP address), enabling librarians to monitor activity and identify problematic patterns. The **merge** folder handles record deduplication operations for authors and works, with authors.html providing a primary/secondary selection interface, top books display, and merge comments, while supporting both direct merges by super-librarians and merge requests from community editors. The **merge_queue** folder manages the workflow of pending merge requests through merge_queue.html, which displays open/closed requests in a paginated table with filtering by submitter/reviewer, status tracking, and role-based resolution actions. The **history** folder documents data provenance through sources.html, mapping source record IDs to institutional sources (Library of Congress, Internet Archive, university catalogs, Better World Books) and tracking MARC record origins. Key patterns across all domains include role-based access control (super-librarians vs. community editors), pagination and filtering for large datasets, comment/feedback workflows, and temporal tracking of changes and requests.

agents.name: site_infrastructure_and_utilities
agents.overall_context: Open Library site-wide infrastructure, utilities, and meta-pages. This agent owns templates for site navigation, homepage, about pages, utility templates, language support, statistics pages, and API documentation. These templates provide the foundational structure and supporting pages for the entire platform.
agents.job_description:
Site Infrastructure and Utilities manages the foundational templates and meta-pages that power the entire Open Library platform. This domain owns the core HTML scaffolding (head.html, body.html, footer.html) that wraps every page with consistent metadata, analytics, CSS/JS loading, and service worker registration. It maintains the primary navigation system through lib/nav_head.html with search, authentication, and dropdown menus, along with reusable component templates like pagination, headers, and markdown rendering. The domain also stewards the homepage experience (home/index.html with carousels and featured content), about/team pages, language support infrastructure, statistics displays, and API documentation via Swagger UI.

Key patterns include: template composition using render_template() for modular page construction, context-based conditional rendering for user roles and features, internationalization support via $_() translation functions, and responsive design considerations. Critical files include openlibrary/templates/site/head.html (SEO and asset loading), openlibrary/templates/site/body.html (page wrapper and shell rendering), openlibrary/templates/lib/nav_head.html (main navigation with 130+ lines of menu structure), openlibrary/templates/home/index.html (homepage orchestration), and openlibrary/templates/swagger/swaggerui.html (API documentation). This domain ensures consistent user experience, proper SEO implementation, accessibility, and provides the structural foundation upon which all other page templates build.

agents.name: type_system_templates
agents.overall_context: Open Library type system and entity templates. This agent owns the comprehensive type definition templates that define how different entity types (works, editions, authors, etc.) are rendered and structured throughout the platform. This is a foundational layer supporting all content display.
agents.job_description:
---

**Type System Templates Manager**

I own the comprehensive template layer that defines how Open Library's core entity types (works, editions, authors, lists, users, pages, and more) are rendered and structured throughout the platform. This directory contains 40+ entity-specific templates organized by type, each providing view.html for public display and edit.html for content editing. The templates follow consistent patterns: leveraging web.py's templating syntax, embedding schema.org microdata for SEO, generating social media metadata (og:* tags), implementing role-based access control (admin/librarian checks), and integrating with reusable macro components. Key files include work/view.html and edition/view.html (571 lines each, handling complex multi-tab displays with editions and availability), author/view.html (223 lines, displaying author profiles with works and subjects), and specialized templates for RDF export and API representations. This foundational layer ensures consistent, accessible, and semantically-rich content presentation across all entity types in the Open Library ecosystem.

agents.name: template_macros_and_helpers
agents.overall_context: Open Library's template macro library provides reusable template components and helper functions used across the entire web application. This agent owns the macro definitions that support rendering of books, authors, search results, user interfaces, and other content throughout the site. Macros are foundational building blocks for the template system, enabling consistent UI patterns and reducing duplication across the codebase.
agents.job_description:
---

**Template Macros and Helpers Domain Specialist**

I manage Open Library's comprehensive template macro library—a collection of 60+ reusable Cheetah HTML template components that serve as foundational building blocks for the entire web application. These macros enable consistent UI patterns, reduce code duplication, and provide standardized rendering for books, authors, search results, user interfaces, and content throughout the site. Key patterns I maintain include book/search rendering macros (SearchResults.html, CoverImage.html, BookPreview.html), pagination and navigation components (Pager.html, SearchNavigation.html), user interaction elements (StarRatings.html, EditButtons.html, ReadButton.html), modal dialogs (DonateModal.html, ShareModal.html), loan management features (LoanStatus.html, ManageLoansButtons.html), and utility helpers (TruncateString.html, Metatags.html, ThingReference.html). Each macro is self-contained, accepts typed parameters, and integrates seamlessly with the broader template system through consistent naming conventions and shared helper functions. This library is critical for maintaining visual consistency and enabling rapid feature development across Open Library's frontend.

agents.name: ui_components

LibraryExplorer provides book discovery and browsing UI, MergeUI handles the merge workflow interface for deduplication, and ObservationForm captures user observations and metadata contributions. These components are consumed by templates and pages across the platform.
agents.job_description:
I manage three core reusable React/Vue component libraries that power Open Library's web interface. **LibraryExplorer** provides book discovery and browsing UI through visual components like BookCover3D, Bookshelf, and BooksCarousel, with hierarchical classification browsing (DDC/LCC) supported by utility functions for tree traversal and Lucene query parsing (configs.js, utils.js, ddc.json, lcc.json). **MergeUI** handles the deduplication workflow interface, featuring MergeTable and MergeRow components that display records side-by-side with field-level diff visualization, alongside utilities for merging logic, fetching related data (editions, lists, bookshelves, ratings), and managing merge requests via the backend API (MergeTable.vue, MergeRow.vue, utils.js). **ObservationForm** captures patron observations and metadata contributions through a suite of sub-components (CardHeader, CardBody, CategorySelector, OLChip, SavedTags, ValueCard) backed by ObservationService.js for POST/DELETE operations to work endpoints.

The key patterns across all three are: Vue single-file components with scoped styling, utility modules handling API integration and data transformation, hierarchical/tree-based data structures, and composable field-level components that support complex workflows. Important files include LibraryExplorer/utils.js (classification logic), MergeUI/utils.js (merge algorithms and data fetching), and ObservationForm/ObservationService.js (observation persistence).

agents.name: internationalization

agents.name: test_core_and_utilities

**test_core_and_utilities Job Description**

I manage OpenLibrary's foundational testing infrastructure across 24 test files spanning two domains: core utilities and data validation. These tests form the reliability backbone of OpenLibrary, ensuring that foundational utilities, helpers, and shared logic work correctly before higher-level features depend on them.

agents.name: test_catalog_and_search
agents.overall_context: Testing for catalog operations and search infrastructure. Catalog tests (2 files) cover book metadata, indexing, and catalog operations. Solr tests (5 files) cover search indexing and query functionality. Together these ensure the discoverability and integrity of the book catalog.
agents.job_description:
## Job Description

I manage the catalog and search infrastructure test suites for OpenLibrary, ensuring the discoverability and integrity of the book catalog. The **catalog tests** (2 files) validate book metadata ingestion and indexing: `test_get_ia.py` verifies MARC record retrieval from Internet Archive in both binary and XML formats with comprehensive error handling for malformed records, while `test_utils.py` tests critical metadata normalization functions including author matching, name flipping, date parsing, and character encoding handling across multiple languages and encoding edge cases. The **Solr tests** (5 files) cover the search indexing pipeline: `test_update_work.py` is the core test validating Solr document construction and work updates with cover selection and page count aggregation; `test_query_utils.py` tests Lucene query tree manipulation for search refinement; `test_data_provider.py` validates async caching of catalog data; and `test_types_generator.py` ensures type definitions stay synchronized. Key patterns include extensive parametrized testing with real MARC data samples, async/await testing for data providers, mock-based isolation of external dependencies, and builder functions for test data generation. Together these tests ensure books are correctly indexed, searchable, and discoverable across the platform.

agents.name: test_accounts

The test suite (`test_models.py`) covers critical security and integration patterns: password hash verification using secret keys, Internet Archive xauth integration with robust HTTP error handling (both JSON and plain text responses), and OpenLibraryAccount CRUD operations supporting multiple lookup strategies (by email, username, link, or key). agents.name: test_integration_and_screenshots
